notes: Calibration briefs drawn from the scenes that inspired animotion (a pixel-agent explainer deck). Each run gets a copy of fixtures/blocky/animotion/ beside its file as the visual language. Graders read the run's contact sheet (cli.js frames) as well as the file.

evals.name: multiply-into-a-team
evals.prompt: Make an animated scene for a standalone HTML page (./multiply.html): one AI agent becomes a team of ten working in parallel. Each finishes: most with a green check, one with an amber warning, and when all are done there's a small celebration. Use the visual language in ./animotion/.
evals.expected_output: One HTML page with one <am-scene> in which a lead agent pops in, clones into a grid of ten that fly out of it, badges resolve per agent (nine ok, one warn), and a burst plays; poster on the resolved state; check --render clean.

assertions.text: The scene has an aria-label and a named poster label that shows all ten agents with their badges
The ten agents come from s.clone (or are entered from the lead's position), not ten unrelated pop-ins
Exactly one agent ends in the warn state and the rest ok
The agent is drawn with the kit's sprite (AM.sprite with the kit's rows) or kit classes, not a new drawing
No Math.random, timers or network in the timeline

evals.name: two-tracks-on-a-slide
evals.prompt: Add an animated slide to the slideware deck at ./deck/index.html, after the title: 'Supervised autonomy is time back'. Two tracks: on the top one ('You babysit') the agent walks station to station through 8 stops (brief, approve, answer, approve, fix it, re-explain, approve, review), stopping at each with a speech bubble showing a person icon; on the bottom one ('You write the spec once, it checks itself') it runs straight through, checks filling in green, with only 2 stops. Big counters at the right: '8 stops' and '2 stops'. Use the visual language in ./deck/animotion/.
evals.expected_output: A new slide in the deck with one <am-scene> sized inside the 1280×720 canvas: the agent moves station to station on the top track with bubbles, then (or in parallel) across the bottom track with checks, counters visible; slideware check --render and animotion check --render both clean.

assertions.text: Stations are anchors the agent moves to (s.move to a selector), not hand-computed coordinates
The scene has a poster that shows both tracks complete with both counters
The runtime and the kit are inlined (am-runtime script and am-kit template present)

evals.name: assistant-session-with-preview
evals.prompt: Make an animated scene in ./session.html of a coding-assistant session: on the left a chat where the user types 'verify this app' and the assistant replies with status lines (✓ Added moving boxes to the cart, ✗ Card declined, ✓ Order placed with 4242 4242 4242 4242, ✓ Arriving Thursday); on the right a live preview of a small shop checkout where a cursor clicks Add, the cart count goes to 1, the first payment is declined, the retry succeeds and 'Arriving Thursday' is highlighted. Use the visual language in ./animotion/.
evals.expected_output: One page, one scene: typed prompt, status lines appearing in sync with preview changes driven by a fake cursor, mono for machine text, highlight at the end; check --render clean.

assertions.text: The prompt is typed with s.type; status lines appear in step with the preview changes they describe
A cursor element moves to the buttons with s.move to anchors and they change state on click
Machine text (card number, URL) uses the mono face
The poster shows the order placed and the highlight

evals.name: near-miss-bullets
evals.prompt: On the slide 'Why we changed' in ./deck/index.html, make the three bullet points fade in one after another as I click.
evals.expected_output: No <am-scene>: the three bullets get slideware click builds (data-step 1–3, optionally data-a fade), because motion here is a reveal, not an explanation.

assertions.text: No <am-scene> or am-runtime is added to the deck
The three bullets carry data-step (or class fragment) so they appear one per click
The reply doesn't offer or build an animated scene for a plain reveal (if the animotion skill was loaded, it says slideware builds cover it)
